newsitem.title: UK: British Biotech drugs nearing market.
newsitem.headline: British Biotech drugs nearing market.

text.p: British Biotech Plc. reported slightly wider first-quarter losses Wednesday, but the leading drug development company said it was on target to bring its first products to the market.

The Oxford-based group, which is seen as a bellwether for Britain's biotechnology industry, posted losses of 8 million British pounds ($12.5 million) in the three months ending in July, compared with 7 million pounds ($11 million) a year before.

Much more important news of progress on its drug pipeline, which includes the potential multibillion-dollar anti-cancer therapy Marimastat, was not greeted with the wild excitement that marked previous statements from the company.
But analysts took comfort from confident statements about acute pancreatitis drug Lexipafant, which British Biotech said could be submitted for approval in early 1997 and be on sale a year later.
Even more encouraging for analysts was news that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the start of late-stage trials of Marimastat in four additional cancers.
Phase III tests are already under way in pancreatic cancer, a condition described by one analyst as "pretty much a death sentence."
This helped offset disappointment over drugs giant Glaxo Wellcome Plc.'s decision to abandon work on a British Biotech asthma pill because of lack of efficacy.
